design.what: git-history evidence that the scoring pipeline this paper measures is not a fixed artifact -- it changes version to version, including in exactly the dimension this paper studies (readable vs. silent failure)
design.method: targeted shallow-fetch of specific tags (not a full unshallow) against the already-vendored clone, then git diff/log restricted to the two files this project's own scoring code imports

referenced_prs: #3708 Fix MultiChoiceRegexFilter.find_match IndexError on all-empty capture groups
findings.what_changed: match = [m for m in match if m][0] -- an uncaught IndexError when the filtered list is empty (every captured group was an empty string) -- became a guarded check that falls back to the sentinel instead of raising.
findings.consequence: A response whose regex captures an all-empty-string tuple used to CRASH the harness on this version; on the pinned version it silently becomes a recorded wrong answer. The extraction PATTERN did not change -- only what happens when it degenerately matches did.

findings.affects: MATH-Hard boxed extraction (this project's scripts/19, 42, 47 -- the leaderboard re-scoring the 90.2% headline is computed on)
what_changed: last_boxed_only_string: 'no boxed answer found' changed from returning None to returning the string sentinel INVALID_ANSWER = '[invalidanswer]'.
remove_boxed: a previously UNCAUGHT AssertionError on malformed \boxed{} syntax is now caught and converted to the same INVALID_ANSWER sentinel.
is_equiv: the symbolic-equivalence timeout tightened from 5 seconds to 1 second.
The equivalence backend itself changed from plain sympy (parse_latex) to a new dependency, math_verify (LatexExtractionConfig, parse, verify).
findings.consequence: Finding 1: the None-vs-sentinel distinction this paper's theorem relies on (a readable failure a caller can branch on, versus an opaque value that flows into downstream comparisons) is itself unstable across versions of the SAME file in the SAME repository. Finding 2: a 5x tighter symbolic-equivalence timeout means more boundary-case comparisons are marked 'not equivalent' (scored wrong) purely because verification took too long, independent of mathematical content -- this project's own load_math_utils (scripts/19) documents that a timeout is treated as non-equivalence, matching the harness's own SIGALRM behavior.
findings.not_attempted: Empirical re-scoring under the pre-drift version, which would require installing its era's plain-sympy dependency rather than the pinned version's math_verify package -- deferred as future work rather than attempted as a risky unattended dependency change.
